title: Institutional Variation in Child Maltreatment Reporting
affiliations: Duke University, University of Michigan at Ann Arbor, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Economics, Finance, Accounting (EFA), Cornell University, University of Michigan at Ann Arbor and University of Michigan School of Social Work

detail.title: Institutional Variation in Child Maltreatment Reporting
detail.abstract:
Involvement with the child welfare system varies dramatically across places. While some of this variation may reflect differences in underlying maltreatment risk, it may also result from differences in institutional responses to similar circumstances. To disentangle these explanations, we study Michigan public school data linked to Child Protective Services reports from 2017–2024. School-level reporting rates range from virtually none to more than half of students reported between kindergarten and fifth grade. We estimate school-specific reporting tendencies using value-added methods and document substantial variation in reporting behavior after accounting for differences in student risk. Using student movers, we show that these estimates are forecast-unbiased. Our estimates imply that school-specific reporting practices account for roughly 40 percent of the variation in reporting rates across schools. We then estimate a structural model that decomposes reporting practices into diagnostic skill and preferences. Differences in skill explain more than twice as much variation as differences in preferences, and higher-reporting schools tend to be more skilled at identifying high-risk cases. Counterfactual simulations imply that improving detection skill would yield significant welfare gains, while recent policy proposals aimed at reducing or equalizing reporting rates generally lower welfare by increasing the number of high-risk cases that go unreported.

title: Cross-Interaction Derivability:From Output Safety to Auditable AI Trajectories
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Cross-Interaction Derivability:From Output Safety to Auditable AI Trajectories

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being evaluated through units that are too small for the systems now being built. Persistent memory, long-horizon tasks, tool use, and autonomous or multi-agent interaction shift the relevant object of audit from the isolated output to the trajectory through which traces are retained, selected, transformed, weighted, and eventually translated into intervention. The distinction rests on an order-of-observation premise: output properties can be assessed at first order (O1), whereas derivability begins at second order and beyond (O2+), because its object is the reconstructable relation among states and transformations rather than the endpoint itself. This paper introduces cross-interaction derivability as a distinct epistemic property of persistent and agentic AI systems: the capacity to reconstruct the materially relevant path through which distributed evidence acquires sufficient authority to justify consequential action. Derivability is distinguished from explainability, provenance, logging, and traceability. The paper argues that privacy of content does not entail derivability of intervention; that gating and threshold-setting are not merely technical operations but distributions of epistemic authority; and that a minimum evidence path may permit selective opacity of content while preserving contestability. It also develops the notion of epistemic compression: the possibility that better localization of consequential transitions can improve auditability while reducing unnecessary search, evaluation overhead, latency, compute, and energy demand. Finally, the paper connects trajectory auditing to responsibility, regulation, and the contemporary crisis of trust surrounding frontier AI. Its claim is deliberately narrow: novelty does not lie in persistent memory, provenance, or longitudinal monitoring as such, but in treating derivability across interactions as a distinct property and the trajectory-not the isolated output, memory item, or agent-as the primary object of audit.

title: One Click Away: AI Tutoring with Khanmigo in a Two-Year School Experiment
affiliations: University of Toronto - Department of Economics and

detail.title: One Click Away: AI Tutoring with Khanmigo in a Two-Year School Experiment
detail.abstract:
Generative AI has been promoted as the technology that could transform education by providing every student a personal tutor. We provide some of the first large-scale experimental evidence, from a two-year cluster randomized trial in 18 Tennessee middleschools in which randomly assigned students used Khan Academy with its AI tutor, Khanmigo, configured to coach rather than give answers, during existing daily remedial mathematics sessions. Assignment raises math achievement by 1.3 national percentile ranks per term, or about 0.06 to 0.08 standard deviations over a school year; the implied effect of a full year of active participation reaches 0.14 standard deviations. These gains resemble those from Khan Academy practice without AI assistance. One explanation is that students used the tutor infrequently and, when they did, rarely engaged it in substantive mathematical dialogue: 96 percent of students tried Khanmigo at least once, but the median student messaged it on only a third of the days they practiced, and in only 17 percent of the exercise sessions in which they made a mistake. Messages that students did send were mostly bare answers or clicks on suggested prompts. The binding constraint appears to be engagement: realizing the promise of AI tutoring will require getting students to use it, not just giving them access.

title: Making AI Tutoring Productive: Evidence from a Mastery-Based Math Practice Experiment
affiliations: University of Toronto - Department of Economics, University of Toronto at Mississauga, University of Pennsylvania and

detail.title: Making AI Tutoring Productive: Evidence from a Mastery-Based Math Practice Experiment
detail.abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) can make tutoring more scalable, but only if students use them to reason through mistakes rather than avoid effort. We study this question in a randomized field experiment with more than 6, 000 middle-school students in Hamilton County Schools using NUMI, a research-based computer-assisted learning (CAL) platform. Students were randomized to AI versus CAL-only support, mastery versus non-mastery progression, and one of two math topics. One week later, they completed a delayed assessment covering practiced and unpracticed material. AI students progressed more slowly and attempted fewer questions, but answered more accurately conditional on reaching an attempt. The clearest mechanism appeared after mistakes: AI improved next-attempt correctness and reduced attempts needed to return to a correct answer, while increasing time spent on each question receiving structured support. Mastery increased three-correct-in-a-row attainment but did not by itself improve delayed learning. The most encouraging delayed-test evidence appears when AI is embedded in the mastery workflow, with marginally significant gains concentrated on practiced Exercise 1 material. The results suggest that LLM tutoring can add value over standard CAL, but its value depends on structure that turns mistakes into productive learning moments.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Financial Foundation Models: A Survey
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Carnegie Mellon University and

detail.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Financial Foundation Models: A Survey
detail.abstract: Financial foundation models increasingly support workflows spanning financial question answering, disclosure analysis, forecasting, and decision-making. In these settings, uncertainty may concern whether evidence is valid and available at the relevant time, whether an interpretation is justified, which outcomes remain plausible, or which action is preferred under costs and risk constraints. Because these objects arise at different points in a workflow, uncertainty cannot be reduced to confidence in a final output. We introduce a source-aware framework that distinguishes six sources of uncertainty across evidence and context, model and inference, and outcome and action, while treating agentic workflows as the execution layer through which uncertainty can propagate, change form, or be reduced. We develop a mechanism-based taxonomy grounded in how methods construct or verify uncertainty and reliability representations, and use it to assess their applicability across financial task domains. We further map finance-specific empirical studies across the taxonomy and task domains to characterize the current research landscape. The analysis reveals a literature that remains largely compartmentalized by task, with limited work connecting evidence and reasoning reliability to downstream prediction and constrained action. By connecting where uncertainty arises, how it is represented, and how it bears on downstream decisions, this survey provides a unified foundation for studying and evaluating uncertainty in financial foundation models.

title: Virtual Tutoring with Computer-Assisted Learning: An Experiment in Take-Up and Learning
affiliations: University of Toronto - Department of Economics, University of Toronto and

detail.title: Virtual Tutoring with Computer-Assisted Learning: An Experiment in Take-Up and Learning
detail.abstract:
We explore the efficacy of an online after-school tutoring program that complements teacher-provided computer-assisted learning practice. The aim is to scaffold students struggling with online Khan Academy practice at school with low-cost, one-on-one virtual supervision for about an hour a week at home. In a two-year randomized trial with the Toronto District School Board, teachers identified struggling Grade 4–8 students, whose parents were then randomly offered additional online tutoring to support their practice at home. The main obstacle was participation. Only 45% of assigned students reached a first session in Year 1. After we reframed the invitation and simplified enrollment, initial take-up in Year 2 rose to 83%, though weekly attendance remained below half—not because students dropped out, but because they attended intermittently. On average, the offer raised Khan Academy practice by about 10 minutes per week. This translated to an average gain in math assessment scores of 0.06 SD, with a confidence interval too wide to rule out null or medium-sized gains (ITT 0.055 SD; 95% CI [−0.09, 0.20]). We find a marginally significant gain in math report-card marks (about 0.08 SD; 95% CI [−0.01, 0.17]) and improvements in math satisfaction and enjoyment, with effects larger in Year 2 than in Year 1, consistent with the higher take-up that year. We therefore conclude that the program holds promise, but more is needed to ensure students actually engage with tutors on a regular basis.

title: The Asymmetry Problem: Rule of Law Measurement, Political Risk, and the Misallocation of Capital
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley Law School

detail.title: The Asymmetry Problem: Rule of Law Measurement, Political Risk, and the Misallocation of Capital

publicationDetails.detailsText: American Journal of International Law Unbound (forthcoming 2026)

detail.abstract: Investors, firms, and policymakers rely on rule of law indices to assess political risk. This Essay argues that these measures are directionally biased: they lag and understate institutional deterioration while prematurely recording and overstating recovery. The source is partly institutional and partly methodological. Rule of law decline can be accomplished rapidly through concentrated legal and political change, whereas restoration must proceed through damaged institutions and across electoral cycles. Composite annual indices, however, average discrete changes across dimensions, rely heavily on formal inputs and perceptions, and therefore smooth concentrated decline while crediting reforms before they produce institutional outcomes. Hungary illustrates the resulting dormancy problem: capital can remain in place while institutional risk accumulates beneath gradually declining scores. Poland illustrates the converse: indices can register electoral turnover and early reform signals as recovery before captured institutions have been rebuilt. These errors distort political risk pricing, cross-border transaction design, firms’ adaptive strategies, and capital allocation. They may also obscure deterioration when investors substitute international enforcement for domestic courts. Drawing on the post-2008 reform of credit-rating oversight, the Essay proposes supplementing composite scores with event-level data, disclosing methods for independent validation, and expressly acknowledging directional bias.

title: A Four Year Case Study of Youth Led Financial and Economic Education for Children in Bengaluru

detail.title: A Four Year Case Study of Youth Led Financial and Economic Education for Children in Bengaluru
detail.abstract: Financial education is usually discussed in the context of teenagers and adults. I began to wonder whether we were starting too late. Children begin interacting with money much earlier than they begin learning about financial literacy formally. They see their parents buy things, receive money as gifts, ask for things they want and learn that they cannot have everything they want. These experiences may seem simple, but they involve choices, priorities and limited resources. In 2022, when I was thirteen, I started Shape the Future, a student led initiative that provides free educational resources and programmes for children. Over the following four years, the initiative reached approximately 2,000 children, primarily between the ages of six and twelve. Around 540 children were reached through offline programmes conducted across three school settings in Bengaluru. For approximately three years, our team conducted regular Saturday sessions with children. Alongside the offline work, we developed digital lessons covering subjects including Money Management, Economics, Law and Indian Politics. This paper documents my experience of building and delivering the programme. I focus on how I approached financial and economic education for younger children, why I chose to begin with simple concepts such as money, needs and wants, and barter, and what I learned from moving between classroom teaching and digital learning. This is an exploratory case study rather than an impact evaluation. I did not conduct a controlled experiment or collect enough longitudinal data to claim that the programme caused measurable changes in financial knowledge or behaviour. Instead, I use the experience of developing and sustaining the programme to examine what early financial and economic education can look like when it is created and delivered by a young person and sustained through regular engagement with children. The experience has changed the way I think about financial education. I no longer believe that it needs to begin with banking, investing or complicated financial products. I think it can begin much earlier with questions children already understand. What is money? What do I need? What do I want? Why can I not buy everything I want? These questions are simple, but they can become the foundation for understanding more complicated financial and economic ideas later.

title: Understanding Students' Non-Use of ChatGPT: Attitudes, Concerns, and Recommendations
affiliations: and Kwantlen Polytechnic University

detail.title: Understanding Students' Non-Use of ChatGPT: Attitudes, Concerns, and Recommendations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests or conflicts of interest related to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable

detail.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT become increasingly integrated into higher education, research has largely focused on students who actively use these technologies, while the perspectives of non-users remain underexplored. Using descriptive frequency analysis of survey responses, this study examines the attitudes, perceptions, and concerns of 37 university students who do not use ChatGPT for academic purposes. The findings are organized into four areas: reasons for non-use, concerns about AI use, factors that may encourage future adoption, and overall perceptions of ChatGPT. The most common reasons for non-use were limited familiarity with ChatGPT and low perceived usefulness. The strongest factor that could encourage future adoption was the availability of clear institutional guidelines outlining appropriate AI use. Overall, students' perceptions were cautious but not strongly negative. These findings suggest that non-use may be influenced more by uncertainty, limited guidance, and lack of experience than by outright rejection of AI technologies. Higher education institutions can support responsible AI engagement by implementing structured AI literacy programs, providing practical training, and communicating clear and transparent policies. Future research should employ experimental and longitudinal approaches to examine how AI literacy and policy clarity influence AI adoption, accuracy, and ethical decision-making when students use tools such as ChatGPT.

title: Hidden in the Stack: Shared AI Infrastructure, Common-Mode Failures, and Potential Operational Contagion in Global Banking

detail.title: Hidden in the Stack: Shared AI Infrastructure, Common-Mode Failures, and Potential Operational Contagion in Global Banking
detail.abstract: Shared technology suppliers can create common operational exposure across banks, but public evidence rarely identifies when that exposure becomes a cascade or financial contagion. This paper develops a layered, disclosure-based framework that separates four objects: common exposure, common-mode operational shock, potential operational cascade, and realised financial contagion. The main sample is the complete 2025 Financial Stability Board list of 29 global systemically important banks. The source register contains 44 public disclosures and yields 43 unique institution-supplier relationships involving 17 external suppliers through 20 August 2026. Microsoft reaches 10 banks in the all-stage network and Google eight; however, a production-only sensitivity produces an eight-eight tie, showing that deployment-stage classification changes the apparent leader. Deployment-specific look-through paths expand OpenAI's structural reach from three direct institutions to six. Yet only seven of 43 relationships state criticality, six disclose fallback or substitutability, and one reports exit testing. Missing-edge analysis further shows that only three adversarially placed Google relationships would change the leading supplier, while the same number of undisclosed relationships can move concentration in opposite directions depending on whether missingness favours incumbents or challengers. The evidence therefore supports a propagation-ready topology, not a claim of realised financial contagion. The paper's contribution is to identify the information and network conditions required to move from visible co-exposure to a defensible systemic-risk assessment.

title: Chile and the CPTPP: Trade and Systemic Considerations

detail.title: Chile and the CPTPP: Trade and Systemic Considerations

keywords: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership

detail.abstract: In this note, I consider the value of the CPTPP for Chile in several dimensions: first, as a conventional trade liberalization exercise aimed at securing Chile's position in the "global factory" by aligning its economic framework with the most advanced "operating system" for Globalization V2; and second, as a ticket to having a seat at the table of potentially the most important "club" shaping the rules-based framework for small open economies in the era of machine knowledge capital-Globalization V3. Prior to joining the CPTPP, Chile had free trade agreements in place with all the other original parties. Accordingly, the agreement offered little additional preferential market access for Chile while posing clear risks of some trade-diversion and preference-erosion effects. The gains were predicated on more subtle impacts in areas such as streamlining of rules of origin and thereby facilitating Chilean firms' participation in regional value chains. As the agreement has matured, the rise in the number of parties seeking to accede to the agreement extends the network effects for Chile of being a member. Moreover, as the CPTPP parties move to update the agreement-particularly its digital economy chapter-Chile has a full seat at the table. Finally, as the United States throws up trade barriers, it naturally deflects trade to flow around US barriers, which enhances the value of Chile's membership in the CPTPP (even as it incentivizes additional economies to apply for accession).

title: Language Barrier and Innovation：Evidence from Law on the Standard Spoken and Written Chinese Language of China

detail.title: Language Barrier and Innovation：Evidence from Law on the Standard Spoken and Written Chinese Language of China
detail.abstract: There is relatively little direct evidence in the literature on how lowering language barriers affects innovation. Implementing Law on the Standard Spoken and Written Chinese Language (LCL), a multi-ethnic, multilingual, and multilingual developing country like China, provides an ideal institutional experiment for studying these issues. Based on the diverse language variation and interleaved implementation of local LCL in various provinces in China, this paper empirically tests the impact of lowering language barriers on innovation and explores the main mechanisms. Empirical results show that LCL shock significantly enhances innovation performance in regions with high dialect diversity, mainly reflected in innovation activities measured by non-invention patent applications. This is because such innovation activities rely more on market feedback and communication, making them more susceptible to spoken and written law. Mechanism analysis shows that LCL significantly improves information access levels and promotes labor mobility and entrepreneurship. The core conclusions of this paper are robust under a series of robustness tests. This study provides direct empirical evidence for understanding how lowering language barriers affects innovation.

title: Journalism as (Temporary?) Catalyst for Police Governance Reform Regarding Use of Facial Recognition Technologies: Analysis of the Clearview AI Scandal in Canada
affiliations: Ontario Tech University and University of Ontario Institute of Technology

detail.title: Journalism as (Temporary?) Catalyst for Police Governance Reform Regarding Use of Facial Recognition Technologies: Analysis of the Clearview AI Scandal in Canada

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts
declarations.ethicsApproval: Only publicly available data was used in this study, so no research ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded by the Social Science and Humanities Research Council of Canada (File number 890-2020-0120).

detail.abstract: In January 2020, the New York Times published an article about Clearview AI, an American company whose facial recognition technology utilized a database of billions of images scraped from the internet, that had managed to amass over 600 police services as clients in the United States, without any public scrutiny. This initial story was picked up by journalists worldwide who began asking their local police if they were also using this technology, with news media attention being most intense in Canada, which was eventually revealed to be the second largest market for the product outside the US. In this chapter, we trace the broad contours of legacy news media coverage of the controversy across Canada, using a thematic content analysis to identify the main narrative features that journalists employed in the initial three months after the story broke. The Clearview AI revelations presented an opportunity for Canadian journalists to lean into their role as watchdogs exposing flaws in police oversight that led to what was cast as a national, collective privacy rights violation. While the work of journalists covering this cyber-event contributed to valuable techno-criticism, the complex media-police relationship also tempered that criticism, making room for the legitimation of police use of other now comparatively less controversial forms of facial recognition technologies.

title: Multi‑Speed Convergence in Southeast Asia: Divergent Growth Paths Between Singapore, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the CLMV Bloc

detail.title: Multi‑Speed Convergence in Southeast Asia: Divergent Growth Paths Between Singapore, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the CLMV Bloc
detail.abstract: ASEAN closed ten points of the income gap with high-income economies after 2000. That sentence has been doing work a regional average cannot do. In a population-weighted reading of World Bank GDP per capita at PPP, the ASEAN-10 moved from 16.5 percent of the high-income level in 2000 to 26.1 percent in 2023, at 3.5 percent a year against 1.5 percent in high-income economies. Crosscountry dispersion of log income inside the ten fell. A βcoefficient of growth on initial income is negative, large, and significant. None of that is one process. Singapore started at 167 percent of the high-income mean and ended at 226 percent: frontier pull-away, not catch-up. It holds 0.9 percent of ASEAN's people and 14 percent of ASEAN GDP at market prices. Viet Nam is the only large latecomer that jointly industrialised. Relative income went from 10.5 to 23.5. Agricultural employment fell from 64 to 27 percent. Industry's employment share rose from 12 to 34. High-tech manufactures reached 44 percent of manufactured exports. Broadband reached 23 per 100. Malaysia gained 12 points of relative income and 3 points of relative productivity. Manufacturing's share of Malaysian GDP fell from 31 to 23 percent. That is a plateau of the World Development Report 2024 kind: the farm exit is done, the last mile is not. Indonesia holds 41 percent of ASEAN's people and closed all four clocks we define-income, productivity, technology, and structure-without occupying Viet Nam's intensive margin. Manufacturing's share of Indonesian GDP fell. High-tech manufactures are 9 percent. Broadband is 5 per 100. Self-employment is 53 percent. CLMV, the Cambodia-Lao PDR-Myanmar-Viet Nam bloc, went from 7.5 to 17.7 percent of high-income income. Drop Viet Nam and CLM went from 3.9 to 10.3. After 2010 the split is sharper: Viet Nam at 4.9 percent a year, CLM at 3.2, Myanmar at 2.5 after a 2000s boom and a 2021 collapse. Treating ASEAN as one convergence club is how Singapore's pull-away and Viet Nam's industrialisation get averaged into a regional success that Malaysia only partly had, that Indonesia had at scale without the factory intensity, and that Myanmar did not have.

title: Asia’s Capital Century — How Sovereign Funds, Domestic Savings, and Regional Financial Integration are Reshaping Global Investment Flow

detail.title: Asia’s Capital Century — How Sovereign Funds, Domestic Savings, and Regional Financial Integration are Reshaping Global Investment Flow
detail.abstract:
This report examines the fundamental forces driving the recalibration of global investment flows toward Asian markets. Through a systemic and quantitative lens, the research analyzes how regional sovereign wealth funds and massive domestic savings pools are being mobilized to finance long-term infrastructure, capital-intensive energy transitions, and technological autarky.

By employing advanced multi-agent model orchestration, the analysis demonstrates how rapid technological diffusion and digital infrastructure investments are drastically accelerating supply chain efficiencies and broad-based economic elevation across emerging economies. Furthermore, the report highlights the accelerated deployment of de-dollarization frameworks, cross-border settlement networks, and bilateral swap agreements. These mechanisms are establishing resilient, parallel financial architectures designed to mitigate exogenous macroeconomic shocks and geopolitical decoupling pressures.

Ultimately, the findings reveal a self-reinforcing capital network—characterized by robust geometric topologies—that structurally reduces reliance on traditional Western capital markets and cements a new era of regional financial multipolarity.

title: A Context-Aware Data Reliability Frameworks for AI-Based Decision Making in Critical Infrastructure

detail.title: A Context-Aware Data Reliability Frameworks for AI-Based Decision Making in Critical Infrastructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The author has no personal or financial relationships with any organizations that could have influenced this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, animals, or patient data. All data used in this research were obtained from publicly available datasets (BUSI - Breast Ultrasound Images Dataset). Therefore, no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Critical infrastructure is now relying more and more on artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision systems to assist with prediction, monitoring, threat detection, and operational control. Nevertheless, the reliability of the data used to make these decisions can vary greatly depending on the operational conditions, the source of the data, its temporal features, environmental changes, and the extent to which it is affected by cyber and other threats. Although recent research has made progress in the areas of context-aware AI, predictive analytics, cybersecurity, and intelligent infrastructure, the various bodies of work are still disjointed when it comes to how data reliability should be continuously evaluated both before and during AI-assisted decision-making (Leyli-Abadi et al., 2025; Mhapsekar et al., 2024; Violos et al., 2025). The present article therefore looks at how context-aware data reliability can be integrated into AI decision systems for critical infrastructure and proposes an integrated conceptual framework for reliability-aware decision-making. To achieve this, the study uses a systematic literature review combined with the development of a conceptual framework, bringing together the findings from research on AI, data quality, context awareness, cybersecurity, predictive analytics, and resilient infrastructure. The synthesis reveals several interrelated dimensions of data reliability, such as accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, provenance, contextual relevance, and security, and shows that reliability cannot be properly established just at the time of data collection. On the contrary, reliability has to be dynamically assessed in light of evolving operational contexts and the specific requirements of the decisions being made (Aziz and Afzal, 2024; Mandaliya and Kulkarni, 2025; Cardenas et al., 2025). The proposed framework places context-aware reliability assessment at an intermediate stage between data acquisition and AI-supported decision-making. The study concludes that such mechanisms can enhance decision confidence, enable earlier warnings, improve responsiveness to cybersecurity threats, ensure operational continuity, and increase the overall resilience of critical infrastructure.

title: Trust as Resolution Infrastructure: Value Preservation, Creditor Coordination, and Bankruptcy Service Trusts in China

detail.title: Trust as Resolution Infrastructure: Value Preservation, Creditor Coordination, and Bankruptcy Service Trusts in China
detail.abstract: Bankruptcy service trusts have become an increasingly common component of large corporate restructurings in China. Among the 144 listed companies whose reorganization plans were approved by courts between 2007 and 2025, the share of plans repaying creditors with trust beneficial interests rose from 4 percent over 2019-2022 to 36 percent in 2024 and 40 percent in 2025. Yet the economic contribution of these trusts is easily misstated: restructuring plans may treat trust units as debt satisfaction while underlying assets remain unmonetized, whereas evaluations based only on immediate cash ignore the value of avoiding forced sales. This paper first develops a two-period model of deferred disposition in which the fire-sale discount, expected asset recoverability, and governance-dependent agency costs jointly determine when a service trust preserves value; four hypotheses follow as comparative statics, including a net-effect boundary for asset complexity. It then combines a censusbased sampling frame compiled from public plan records and professional annual reports, a sourcegraded audit of 20 cases, a focal positive mechanism analysis of the Founder Group restructuring, and a structured comparison of the 2024 listed-company cohort. Of the 20 audited cases, 12 have a verified plan, seven a verified establishment, and only two provide case-level monetary evidence meeting the audit threshold: Bohai Steel reports cumulative cash distributions, while HNA Group's trust units are reported at a Level 3 fair-value carrying amount in affiliated companies' audited financial statements. Because realized trust distributions remain sparse, the paper specifies a package-level market-implied recovery measure and an exploratory roadmap of three prospective research designs built on the 2023 trust-business classification reform, the 2024 Supreme People's Court and CSRC Minutes, and withincase creditor-class variation, stating explicitly the conditions under which each would support causal inference. The evidence to date supports an institutional conclusion: where viable operations can be TRUST AS RESOLUTION INFRASTRUCTURE 2 separated from difficult but potentially recoverable assets, a service trust preserves contingent creditor rights and allows the core restructuring to close without a forced sale. Whether it raises discounted recovery is the empirical hypothesis this design makes testable and auditable.

title: Sudan: Analyzing the Complexities of Polarization and Terrorism
affiliations: Al-Neelain University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Sudan: Analyzing the Complexities of Polarization and Terrorism

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I am a Sudanese scientist and a victim of civil war
declarations.ethicsApproval: There is no conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: No Funding

detail.abstract: Sudan, a nation of profound strategic significance at the crossroads of Africa and the Arab world, offers a critical case study in the intersection of internal political polarization, international terrorism designation, and geopolitical entanglement. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of Sudan's trajectory from its designation as a State Sponsor of Terrorism (SST) in 1993 through its contentious normalization with Israel under the Abraham Accords, culminating in the civil war that has produced the world's worst contemporary humanitarian catastrophe. Drawing on World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) economic data, the analysis demonstrates how the SST designation functioned not merely as diplomatic censure but as a structural constraint on economic development, contributing to squandered oil revenues and perpetuating fragility (World Bank Group, 2023; France 24, 2018). The paper argues that the 2020 normalization agreement, rather than representing a strategic reorientation, constituted a tactical maneuver by military elites seeking international legitimacy and sanctions relief, occurring alongside deepening entanglement with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Muslim Brotherhood (Jerusalem Center for Security and Foreign Affairs, 2026; Ynetnews, 2026). Using newly generated visual models of Sudan's fragility cycle and dual-track foreign policy, this study contributes to understanding how authoritarian persistence, economic isolation, and instrumentalized external partnerships sustain polarization.

title: From Water to Resource: A Multi-Actor Techno-Economic Assessment for the Offshore Wind End-of-Life Supply Chain
affiliations: University of Antwerp, Ghent University, University of Antwerp and University of Antwerp - Department of Engineering Management

detail.title: From Water to Resource: A Multi-Actor Techno-Economic Assessment for the Offshore Wind End-of-Life Supply Chain
detail.abstract: The end-of-life phase of offshore wind farms is moving rapidly from a future concern to an operational reality, yet techno-economic assessments still largely stop at offshore removal. As a result, the economic role of ports, recycling, and secondary material markets remains poorly understood. This study addresses this gap by operationalizing Multi-Actor Techno-Economic Assessment (MATEA) for the full end-of-life supply chain, expanding its actor scope to include the recycling company, offshore wind farm operator, and marine contractor. Using process modeling and industry data, the framework is applied to a Belgian offshore wind farm assessing eleven combined offshore and onshore decommissioning scenarios. The results show that recycling companies can generate positive scrap offers from approximately €600 to €71,400/MW, driven primarily by removed mass, offshore timing, and ferrous metal and copper prices. For the offshore wind farm operator, net decommissioning costs remain dominated by offshore operations and range from approximately €141,000 to €436,000/MW, with onshore processing choices exerting only marginal influence. The analysis reveals a tight coupling between offshore execution and onshore feasibility, whereby removal strategies and campaign duration directly shape port occupation, recycling costs, and scrap value recovery. While material recovery generates downstream revenues, these revenues remain insufficient to cover offshore decommissioning costs in any scenario. By quantifying these interactions from water to resource, the operationalized MATEA framework provides a transparent basis for evaluating circular end-of-life supply-chain strategies and highlights coordination, rather than recycling technology, as the central challenge for circular offshore wind practices.

title: A Study on the Long-Term Trend of Sovereign Currency Exchange Rates

detail.title: A Study on the Long-Term Trend of Sovereign Currency Exchange Rates

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involves no human-subject data and requires no ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
The development of exchange rate theories is demarcated by the Mundell-Fleming model. Prior to this, the balance of payments approach remained fixated on current account equilibrium, completely neglecting the capital and financial account. In contrast, post-Mundell-Fleming exchange rate determination theories established the dominant role of the capital and financial account, attempting to explain exchange rate fluctuations through price signals such as interest rates, inflation, and income levels. The author argues that price signals are essentially the outcomes of economic operations, whereas a country's competitive advantage in the international markets for goods, services, and assets constitutes the fundamental driver of exchange rate movements.

This paper endeavors to break free from the theoretical framework of exchange rate determination theories by adjusting the balance of payments identity and de-emphasizing the distinction between the current account and the capital and financial account. It establishes the central role of the exchange rate in balancing international payments within the identity, completing a closed-loop process: (1) localized changes lead to an imbalance in the identity; (2) the identity imbalance triggers exchange rate adjustments; (3) exchange rate changes influence overall variations; (4) overall variations offset the initial localized changes. Furthermore, the rate of exchange rate change is expressed as the ratio of the imbalance magnitude in the balance of payments identity to the exchange rate elasticity.

Finally, by analyzing the fundamental and non-fundamental factors underlying the competitive advantages of Chinese and American goods, services, and assets in international markets, the paper assesses the long-term trend of the RMB/USD exchange rate.

title:
What Does a Cognitive Discount Factor Measure? 
Housing Illiquidity and the Governmental Production of Bounded Rationality in South Korea

detail.title:
What Does a Cognitive Discount Factor Measure? 
Housing Illiquidity and the Governmental Production of Bounded Rationality in South Korea
detail.abstract: Behavioural macroeconomics commonly reports how steeply agents discount the future as a structural parameter. This article asks what such a parameter measures and develops two independent arguments that it need not measure a property of the mind. The first is external: if rationality is ecological in Simon's and Gigerenzer's sense, and government operates by arranging the milieu in Foucault's sense, then bounded-rationality parameters are governable variables. The second is immanent: behavioural heterogeneous-agent models do not assign the parameter a determinate bearer. It can be attached to a household planner or to the individuals represented by that planner, and can be observationally equivalent to an information structure or a population share; moreover, it binds only on asset-holding households. South Korea supplies the determination that the aggregate framework withholds. Housing illiquidity is specified as a technology acting on the temporal structure of decision, while a genealogy of four technologies-the jeonse deposit, asset-based welfare, transaction control, and calibrated classification-traces how that milieu was assembled. The cognitive discount factor is therefore a governmental artefact: housing policy is also policy about cognitive horizons. Five testable implications are proposed through which the account can be contested.

title: Thorin Measures and the Reciprocal Xi Function
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Thorin Measures and the Reciprocal Xi Function
detail.abstract: A Hadamard product is a Thorin transform: the atoms of the Thorin measure sit at the shifted zeros, and Bondesson's criterion for the class of generalized gamma convolutions becomes the requirement that those atoms be real and positive. We develop this dictionary for quasi-infinitely divisible laws, allowing signed and complex Thorin measures, prove uniqueness of the representing measure by a Cauchy transform argument, and show that positivity of the Thorin measure is membership of the underlying entire function in the Laguerre Pólya class. Two instances are the Pólya Gamma law of Bayesian data augmentation, where the entire function is cosh, and the Riemann xi function. Applied to L ξ (θ) = ξ (1/2)/ξ (1/2 + √ 2θ) the dictionary separates into an unconditional layer and one hypothesis. Unconditionally, L ξ is the Laplace transform of an infinitely divisible law H ξ , the time one marginal of a driftless subordinator, which forms a Wald couple with the Pólya Wintner variable and a van Dantzig pair with H ξ N; and no finite truncation of the complete monotonicity criterion has content, since every alternating cumulant condition, and every derivative condition up to order 8 × 10 10 , holds without hypothesis. The Riemann hypothesis is exactly the remaining step: it holds if and only if H ξ is a generalized gamma convolution, with Thorin measure ∑ γ>0 δ γ 2 /2. A second criterion comes from the Lévy to Thorin map, which produces the Thorin measure by Gaussian subordination rather than from the zeros. Its density at σ is a Poisson smoothing of the zero counting measure whose boundary value on the critical line is the atomic measure above, and the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to positivity of that density for σ in (1/2, 1), equivalently to |ξ (σ + iu)|/ξ (σ) being nondecreasing in σ for every u. Unlike the first criterion this one is local, and detects a violation at any height. Along the way: van Dantzig duality is the involution U →-U on Thorin measures; the explicit formula is an identity between a Thorin measure carried by the zeros and a Lévy measure carried by the prime powers; the failure of infinite divisibility of the completed zeta distribution for σ > 1 is caused by exactly one negative Thorin atom, coming from the pole at s = 1, and the same holds for the completed Dedekind zeta function of any number field; and the de Bruijn and Newman constant is the entry time of the Thorin class along a flow that is a Gaussian tilt of the Pólya Wintner law.

title: Developing a New Method to Uncover Skills Trends in Emerging Economies Using Online Data and NLP techniques
affiliations: International Labour Organization (ILO), International Labour Organization (ILO), , Research Department (ILO) and International Labour Organization (ILO)

detail.title: Developing a New Method to Uncover Skills Trends in Emerging Economies Using Online Data and NLP techniques

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The responsibility for opinions expressed in this article rests solely with its authors, and publication does not constitute an endorsement by the International Labour Office of the opinions expressed in it. Other usual disclaimers apply.

detail.abstract: This methodological brief describes an innovative approach that exploits online big data from job vacancies and applicants' profiles and utilizes natural language processing (NLP) to extract information on skills. The approach is based on a taxonomy comprising 15 unique skills subcategories across the broader cognitive, socio-emotional, and manual skills categories. It focuses on skills that are transferable rather than occupation-specific. So far tested with data on Uruguay, Brazil, the Russian Federation, and South Africa, the method is applicable to countries of all income levels and allows detecting country-specific skills trends. It captures a wide range of sectors and occupations, including those requiring manual labour. It can be used to offer novel insights into skills demand, supply and mismatch, as well as into the relationship between skills and aspects of job quality and/or job transitions.

title: Hyperbolic Secant Completeness and the Critical Strip
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Hyperbolic Secant Completeness and the Critical Strip
detail.abstract: Lai and Vere-Jones (1979) pose as their first open problem the completeness of the scale family {sech θx}, prove it under a supplementary hypothesis by Möbius inversion, and ask whether the hypothesis can be relaxed. This paper identifies the obstruction exactly and answers the question. The Mellin transform of sech is 2Γ(s)β(s) and the weights w(r) = (-1) r µ(2r + 1) are the Dirichlet coefficients of 1/L(s, χ 4), so the inversion (8) is a reciprocal L-function in disguise. In the bounded class |f (x)| ≤ Cx c-1 the problem becomes a Wiener-Tauberian nonvanishing condition, in the homogeneous form of Kac (1965), and three things follow. The completeness set is exactly the set of zero free vertical lines of β, and the annihilator on any line is the weak star closed span of the log periodic modes x c-1+iγ indexed by the ordinates of the zeros there. Unconditionally, completeness holds for every c > 0 outside a countable set of measure zero; the exceptional set is symmetric about 1/2, disjoint from [1, ∞), contains 1/2, and any exceptional c carries zeros only at heights ≥ exp{A/(1-c)}. GRH for χ 4 is precisely the statement that the exceptional set is the single self dual exponent c = 1/2. A character criterion sharpens this: every class below L ∞ in the usual scale, each L p with p < ∞ and C 0 among them, gives completeness unconditionally at a single exponent, with Proposition 1 the case p = 1 and the Möbius inversion not needed. The arithmetic appears exactly at p = ∞, where pure characters first fit. The bridge to ζ is the Esscher tilt (e x + 1)-1 = 1 2 e-x/2 sech(x/2), which is Salem's kernel, so Salem's criterion is the completeness problem for the natural exponential family generated by the secant law rather than for the secant density. The tilt introduces one spurious exceptional exponent at c = 1, from the 2-adic factor 1-2 1-s , which is why Salem's range is the open interval (1/2, 1).

title: p(doom)
affiliations: and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: p(doom)
detail.abstract: I. J. Good's 1965 speculation on the first ultraintelligent machine posed a question now traded as a number, p(doom), on which published estimates span four orders of magnitude. We treat the question information-theoretically: the weight of evidence an observation carries about an unrealised event is a log-likelihood ratio whose expectation is a Kullback-Leibler divergence, so the published disagreement is a demand for between five and seven bans of information that no available experiment can supply. The dispute is prior, not posterior: deep uncertainty in Knight's sense dressed as priced risk. The structural arithmetic in circulation is wrong twice over. Risk adds across an exhaustive partition of pathways, where the popular calculators price a single chain. And risk does not multiply across barriers in series, since the probability that all m fail is E[θ m ], governed by a prior concentration c, a monotone reparameterisation of the mutual information between component failures, that nobody elicits. Holding the elicited per-barrier failure probability at 10-3 , four barriers deliver anywhere from 10-12 to 8 × 10-4 , and the 1961 Goldsboro accident carries 4.9 bans against independence. Two observations would move the number rather than the rhetoric: the breach depth of safety incidents, and evidence of an independent origin of life.

title: Optimal Tax Smoothing Under Rational Inattention
affiliations: and

detail.title: Optimal Tax Smoothing Under Rational Inattention
detail.abstract: We revisit the canonical tax-smoothing model when fiscal authorities have limited capacity to process information about permanent government spending. Using annual central-government data for 20 OECD economies, we document two empirical patterns: tax rates are highly persistent and predominantly nonstationary, while lagged changes in government expenditure help predict subsequent tax-rate changes. We introduce rational inattention by allowing the government to process information about permanent government spending subject to an informationprocessing constraint. The tax rate remains a martingale with respect to the government's endogenous information set, but limited attention generates delayed tax adjustment from the econometrician's perspective. Limited attention attenuates the initial tax response to government spending innovations, shifts more financing toward debt, and spreads tax adjustment over time. Lower information-processing capacity, through more persistent filtering errors and endogenous signal noise, also raises the relative volatility of tax-rate changes. Crosscountry evidence provides partial support for these implications. Rational inattention improves the relative-volatility prediction in 13 of 20 countries and, in a VAR for government spending and the budget deficit, brings the model-implied coefficients closer to their empirical counterparts in up to 15 countries.

title: Strategic Default as an Optimal Stopping Problem

detail.title: Strategic Default as an Optimal Stopping Problem
detail.abstract: This paper develops a model of sovereign default as an optimal stopping problem, built on real analysis and continuous-time stochastic calculus. A government continuously observes a mean-reverting fiscal capacity index and must decide when, if ever, to stop servicing its debt. We cast the decision as a value function problem, prove existence and uniqueness of the optimal default threshold using the Banach contraction mapping theorem and value function iteration, and characterise the solution via a free-boundary ordinary differential equation with smooth-pasting and value-matching conditions. Comparative statics derived through implicit differentiation show how the threshold responds to interest rates, fiscal volatility, and the reputational cost of default. The framework is applied to the 1998 Russian sovereign default, demonstrating how the collapse of oil revenues and the explosion of GKO yields jointly drove the state process through the critical threshold, making default the value-maximising strategy. Empirical charts of GKO yields, reserve dynamics, the ruble exchange rate, and oil prices validate the model's predictions.

title: The High Middle Ages: A Historiographical Framework
affiliations: Universidad de la Republica

detail.title: The High Middle Ages: A Historiographical Framework
detail.abstract: This study examines the transformation of historical writing in the Latin West between the fifth and eleventh centuries. Its object is not the events of the period, but the operations through which authors and communities selected, ordered, and explained the past. It argues that early medieval Christian historiography did not represent a degradation of classical models, but rather a reorganisation of historical writing: it retained techniques, authorities, and materials inherited from Antiquity and subordinated them to new conceptions of time, community, and legitimacy. The corpus is examined along five axes—conceptions of time, models of causality, selection of sources, narrative genre, and institutional function—applied to Eusebius of Caesarea, Augustine of Hippo, and Orosius as late antique antecedents; to the historians of the post-Roman kingdoms; to Bede; and to the annalistic, chronicle, and hagiographical production of monastic milieux. The Asturian chronicles and selected Andalusi testimonies make it possible to incorporate the specificity of the Iberian Peninsula without subordinating it to Latin periodisation. The study distinguishes three temporal levels and explicitly separates modern interpretive categories from the early medieval corpus.

title: Rethinking Fa Bu Qing Chuan ("The Dharma Should Not Be Transmitted Lightly"): Knowledge Propagation Ethics and Implications for Open Knowledge Platforms

detail.title: Rethinking Fa Bu Qing Chuan ("The Dharma Should Not Be Transmitted Lightly"): Knowledge Propagation Ethics and Implications for Open Knowledge Platforms
detail.abstract: A doctrine of restricted transmission is stated across several traditions and is compactly formulated in the eight-character maxim fa bu qing chuan, dao bu jian mai, holding that the dharma is not transmitted lightly and the way is not sold cheaply. The doctrine appears to stand in opposition to the commitments on which open knowledge platforms, open source practice and the open scholarly record are built, and the opposition is ordinarily settled by dismissing one side. This paper asks what the doctrine asserts, what in it survives examination, who is competent to determine whether a transmission should occur, and which requirements on a transmitter are compatible with open knowledge practice. Transmission is treated as an operation on a system already in some state, and the doctrine's single notion of readiness is separated into representational, dynamical and relational conditions, which differ in who is able to remedy their failure. The readiness assessment is then found to be administered by the party a finding of unreadiness relieves, filtered in its common implementation by a capacity uncorrelated with the disposition it is meant to detect, and insulated from the objection of the party it concerns. A thesis about knowledge whose acquisition consists in a reorganisation of the receiver is retained, and separated from the claim, common to the tradition and unsupported by it, that the reorganisation requires the receiver's suffering. The position advanced replaces the judgement of readiness with three requirements on the transmitter's own conduct: an account of what a transmission affords, of the parties a chosen setting distributes it to, and of the reception failures a chosen form invites; continued attention to what follows; and retention of the means of revising the terms. A justificatory burden is allocated where effects are substantially irreversible, symmetrically across withholding and transmitting. The rights a transmitter retains are treated on a distinction between dominion and custody, so that a commitment against possessing what one has produced constrains authority over its future and leaves intact the standing required to act against exploitation; and the paper states plainly that no course available, including transmitting nothing, supplies a guarantee against misuse. The harms at issue are extended to those arising under unbounded propagation, among them occupation of a subject by an early artifact whose terms obstruct its own repair, and licensing, staged release and administered disclosure intervals are examined against them. The paper advances no further candidate for a single correct account of when knowledge may be passed on, offering a common language in which a doctrine formed under one set of conditions and instruments developed under another may be compared; and it states its own terms together with the conditions under which they would be shown to be mistaken.

title: Recognizing Accountants and Trading Goods

detail.title: Recognizing Accountants and Trading Goods
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the perceived credibility of foreign accounting labor is associated with international goods trade. Accountants support cross-border activity by helping firms monitor foreign operations, assess counterparties, extend trade credit, and write supply contracts. I study this issue using international mutual recognition agreements (MRAs) for professional accountants, which publicly certify the comparability of accounting credentials across jurisdictions. Using a global database of accounting MRAs matched to bilateral manufacturing trade data, I find that goods trade is 18.1 percent higher after an accounting MRA is in place, corresponding to about 4 percent lower inferred bilateral trade costs. The analysis compares trade within the same directional jurisdiction pair over time, and I interpret the evidence as incremental to broader trade-agreement relationships rather than as the isolated causal effect of MRAs alone. Consistent with a credibility interpretation, the association is stronger where foreign-accountant credibility is harder to establish and is accompanied by greater foreign-office activity, foreign employment, and foreign supply-chain contracting. The findings suggest that accounting credential recognition can support goods trade by making foreign accounting labor more credible.

title: Business Influence and the Politics of Remediating Foreign Control in Strategic Infrastructure

detail.title: Business Influence and the Politics of Remediating Foreign Control in Strategic Infrastructure

keywords: Infrastructure Security Foreign Direct Investment Strategic Control Dilemma FDI Screening Securitization Remediation Costs Economic Statecraft Process Tracing National Security

detail.abstract: Why do governments facing foreign involvement in strategic infrastructure sometimes remove the firm, sometimes constrain it, and sometimes preserve the relationship? Structural accounts identify dependence, ownership, and rivalry, but an explanation consistent with an outcome is not necessarily the mechanism that produced it. This article recasts the Strategic Control Dilemma as a two-stage political-economy theory. Control exposure and attributed state leverage explain when a relationship becomes a security problem; correction cost, state-created outside options, and contests over market and technology information explain which remedy becomes feasible and authoritative. The empirical design combines a public-record pilot inventory of 27 host-state–firm–project episodes across telecommunications, ports, electricity, nuclear power, semiconductors, and related critical assets with nested process tracing of the United Kingdom's January-to-July 2020 Huawei reversal and the Hinkley Sizewell nuclear sequence. Rivalry is coded from pre-decision strategy and alliance relations, and the inventory includes Chinese, Russian, allied, and partner-country firms. Outcomes are measured on two axes: functional displacement and instrument coerciveness. This resolves the Sizewell problem: CGN was fully displaced from the final project structure, but through compensated negotiation and state-backed finance rather than a documented prohibition. Actor–claim–transmission matrices show that NCSC's revised assurance judgment changed the direction of Huawei policy, while operator evidence shaped the transition period; at Sizewell, EDF's financing claims and public investment created an outside option through which a politically desired ownership change could occur. Piraeus is retained only as a low-confidence boundary case. The article reports completed public-record evidence separately from a specified interview and archival stage, avoiding claims of influence based on participation alone.

title: Design and Implementation of a Hybrid Economic Expert System for MSMEs in Nigeria

detail.title: Design and Implementation of a Hybrid Economic Expert System for MSMEs in Nigeria
